executiveStoryObjective: Diagnose the self-assessed fraud-control environment, explain its most material patterns and set the first 90-day response.

movements.title: Executive diagnosis
movements.objective: Explain where the organisation stands and what the recorded result means.
movements.transitionPurpose: Show why the score requires a closer look at the few patterns driving it.
movements.requiredManagementTakeaway: Management should understand the result, its uncertainty and immediate priority.

movements.title: What is driving the result
movements.objective: Synthesise deterministic finding clusters into management themes.
movements.transitionPurpose: Move from broad pattern to the findings that matter most.
movements.requiredManagementTakeaway: Leadership should focus on the small number of patterns with the greatest fraud-risk consequence.

movements.title: The findings that matter most
movements.objective: Explain priority weaknesses as advisory observations.
movements.transitionPurpose: Show how linked weaknesses could become plausible fraud pathways.
movements.requiredManagementTakeaway: Each priority weakness needs an owned treatment, not only a description.

movements.title: How exposure could materialise
movements.objective: Narrate the approved conditional fraud pathways.
movements.transitionPurpose: Translate plausible pathways into the first control responses.
movements.requiredManagementTakeaway: Scenarios are conditional pathways that help management test prevention, detection and containment.

movements.title: What management should do first
movements.objective: Set first-priority controls and a readable 30/60/90 response.
movements.transitionPurpose: Close by defining what success should look like after the first response period.
movements.requiredManagementTakeaway: Management should know the first controls, owners, timing and success measures.

movements.title: Management conclusion
movements.objective: Close the diagnosis with a practical next step.
movements.transitionPurpose: End with the management implication and route forward.
movements.requiredManagementTakeaway: Within 90 days the organisation should have accountable ownership, priority controls and a repeatable first operating cycle.

requiredConclusion: Explain what management should recognise, which few changes matter most, what should be true within 90 days and the sensible next step.
prohibitedClaims: invented incident, loss, customer, supplier, system or interview
legal, regulatory, benchmark, certification or guarantee conclusion
